findings.title: Vendor keeps IP in outputs that AtliQ must hand to Rheinwerk Analytics GmbH exclusively
findings.explanation: This agreement lets the vendor retain ownership of its annotation outputs and gives AtliQ only a non-exclusive licence (§7.2). The upstream Rheinwerk Analytics GmbH contract (§6.5, still in review) requires Rheinwerk Analytics GmbH to receive exclusive rights in all work results. AtliQ cannot pass on rights it does not hold. Align the two before either is signed.
findings.contract_quote: Vendor shall retain all right, title and interest in and to its tools, labelling platform, scripts, ontologies, annotation guidelines developed by Vendor, and annotation outputs, including all intellectual property rights therein (collectively, "Vendor IP").

evidence.quote: Except for PipeKit, Client shall acquire the exclusive, perpetual, transferable and unrestricted right of use in all Work Results created specifically for Client, upon full payment of the relevant Milestone Fee.

escalation_hints: Check with Pranav (CTO) — IP reuse, delivery model or staffing.

findings.title: EU personal data with no GDPR sub-processor terms or client consent
findings.explanation: This vendor would process EU personal data (e.g. technician names in maintenance logs) on AtliQ's behalf, making it a GDPR sub-processor. Nothing here flows down DPA terms (Art. 28(4)), and the upstream client contract requires the client's prior written consent to subcontract. AtliQ needs the client's consent and a DPA flow-down with the vendor before any data is shared.
findings.contract_quote: Source data comprises vibration, temperature and pressure sensor streams from End Client customer plants, together with maintenance work orders and technician logs (including technician names, shift identifiers and free-text notes).

evidence.quote: Supplier may subcontract parts of the services only with Client's prior written consent.
evidence.label: Rheinwerk Analytics GmbH draft (C-028) — upstream client contract

evidence.quote: To the extent Supplier processes personal data on behalf of Client, the Parties shall conclude the Data Processing Agreement pursuant to Art.

findings.needs_info: Get the end client's written consent to the sub-processor and add DPA flow-down terms (or anonymise names before sharing).

findings.title: Pay-when-paid: the vendor is paid only after the end client pays AtliQ (long-stop 120 days)
findings.explanation: AtliQ is the buyer. The vendor carries AtliQ's collection risk and may wait up to 120 days. AtliQ's own position as a supplier is '30 days, 45 max'; for PixelCraft (six people) Karandeep agreed 30-day payment. The tracker notes say the vendor is already pushing back on this ('we're 12 people').
findings.contract_quote: AtliQ's obligation to pay any invoice is conditional upon AtliQ's receipt of payment from the End Client for the corresponding services.
escalation_hints: Discuss with the vendor — AtliQ's own paper; PixelCraft precedent shows how it was softened before.

findings.title: AtliQ's paper makes the vendor indemnify AtliQ's own negligence
findings.explanation: The vendor indemnity applies even where AtliQ was negligent. AtliQ refused exactly this from PayTrack ('we can't insure against PayTrack's own negligence').
findings.contract_quote: Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless AtliQ, its Affiliates, and their respective directors, officers, employees, agents, successors and assigns (the "AtliQ Indemnitees") from and against any and all Losses arising out of or relating to (a) the Services or Deliverables, (b) any breach of this Agreement by Vendor, (c) any claim by the End Client relating to the Services or Deliverables, or (d) any act or omission of Vendor Personnel, in each case regardless of whether such Losses are caused in whole or in part by the negligence of any AtliQ Indemnitee.
escalation_hints: Discuss with the vendor — AtliQ's own paper; PixelCraft precedent shows how it was softened before.

findings.title: AtliQ's own paper makes the vendor's liability unlimited while AtliQ's is capped
findings.explanation: AtliQ is the buyer. The vendor's liability is uncapped By contrast §10.2 caps the other side's liability at THE FEES ACTUALLY PAID BY ATLIQ TO VENDOR UNDER THIS AGREEMENT. This is the clause Karandeep refuses from clients ('liability → 1x fees. NOT unlimited') and the one PixelCraft pushed back on — AtliQ agreed then to cap liability at fees for both sides.
findings.contract_quote: NOTHING IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL LIMIT OR EXCLUDE VENDOR'S LIABILITY FOR ANY LOSSES, WHETHER DIRECT OR INDIRECT, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING VENDOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS.
escalation_hints: Discuss with the vendor — AtliQ's own paper; PixelCraft precedent shows how it was softened before.

findings.title: AtliQ's own paper imposes uncapped daily-style delay damages on the vendor
findings.explanation: AtliQ is the buyer here. The delay clause charges the vendor two percent (2%) of Total Fees per day, no cap, no exclusion for client-caused delay, cumulative with other remedies. This is the same structure AtliQ rejects when clients send it (Acme, Northwind, Trustline) and the one that cost AtliQ $9k on Brightwater. With PixelCraft, Karandeep deleted the delay penalty for a six-person agency. Consider whether this term is fair to a small vendor.
findings.contract_quote: If Vendor fails to achieve any Delivery Date, Vendor shall pay AtliQ, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Fees for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.
escalation_hints: Discuss with the vendor — AtliQ's own paper; PixelCraft precedent shows how it was softened before.

findings.title: AtliQ's vendor template still has the terms softened for PixelCraft
findings.explanation: 4 one-sided terms in AtliQ's own paper (delay penalty, payment, uncapped vendor liability) are the same three Karandeep removed for PixelCraft in Oct 2025 — 'I don't want our paper to be the thing I hate receiving'. The fix was made in PixelCraft's copy only; the template was apparently never updated, and this draft was built from it (and, per the tracker, partly from a client's draft). Consider updating the template, not just this agreement.
